entities.summary: Ole Otto Cicin von Paus, known as Ole Paus, was a Norwegian general, diplomat and NATO official. During the Second World War he was an aide-de-camp to the Norwegian commander-in-chief, General Otto Ruge, during the German invasion of Norway in 1940, and was later head of the army group in the military intelligence service of the exile Norwegian High Command in London and thus one of the founders of the Norwegian Intelligence Service. During the Cold War he served as a military attaché in Stockholm and Helsinki during the 1950s, was promoted to general in 1964 and was commander-in-chief in Central Norway from 1964 to 1971.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a key figure in the Norwegian Intelligence Service and commander-in-chief of Central Norway, Ole Paus played a crucial role in maintaining Norway's sovereignty during World War II. His leadership and strategic decisions likely influenced the country's ability to resist German occupation.
